idiom_name: no binding runtime in the mainstream stack; presenter/view-shaped state plus Stimulus values on the client
implementation_notes: Ruby's mainstream stack is server-rendered Rails, where each request builds state once and renders a template: there is no observable view-model and no binder that makes a view react to property changes, so the pattern's defining mechanism is absent rather than merely hand-written. What remains worth keeping is the separation it protects: put display logic in a presenter, decorator or view component instead of the model and template, keep interaction state in Stimulus controllers whose data-*-value attributes the framework reads and observes, and push server-side updates with Turbo Streams. Ruby desktop frameworks exist and can host a real view-model, but they are not the ecosystem's default and must be chosen explicitly.
code_sketch:
# app/presenters/login_presenter.rb   -- view-shaped state, plain Ruby
class LoginPresenter
  def initialize(user) = @user = user
  def submit_label = @user.guest? ? "Sign in" : "Continue"
end
<!-- app/views/sessions/new.html.erb -->
<form data-controller="login">
  <input name="user" data-login-target="user" data-action="input->login#refresh">
  <button><%= LoginPresenter.new(@user).submit_label %></button>
</form>
pitfalls: There is no binding engine on either side: any 'reactive' behaviour is a full request/response cycle or a Turbo Stream, so per-keystroke state must go to a Stimulus controller or round-trip to the server.
Stimulus state lives in the DOM (data-*-value) and disappears on navigation; server state must be re-rendered, so keep a single source of truth or the two diverge.
Hand-rolled observers are leak-prone: blocks capture self, and the observer gem is a Gemfile dependency again (it left the standard library in Ruby 3.0).
View helpers that reach into domain objects recreate the coupling the pattern is meant to remove; presenters must read the model, not mutate it.
alternative: Server-rendered presentation instead: keep view-shaped state in presenters/decorators or a view component, render it from ordinary controller actions, and put client-side interaction in Stimulus controllers (data-*-value + actions) with Turbo Streams for server pushes; reserve a hand-written observer (the observer gem or a PORO with callbacks) for a genuinely long-lived desktop object.
